author.exposure: Product plan, existing catalog and Coherence adoption audit known. Only curation counts, readiness and hashes seen before drafting; no corpus cases or reference answers opened.

common.scope: One named function, file-owned operation or explicitly delimited call boundary. Not a whole-project guarantee.
common.parameterRules: Only fields in the candidate's parameter schema may be bound. Source addresses identify existing data/interfaces/observations; they cannot conceal a new policy algorithm or arbitrary predicate. Descriptive text may explain evidence, not alter clause semantics. An enum cannot be extended to rescue a case. No post-hoc equivalence/input/scope adjustment.
common.assessing: Assess whether the contract faithfully represents a source-grounded responsibility, not whether implementation already fulfills it. A violating implementation may be a fit. Inadequate evidence is unknown; an observed necessary behavior outside this schema is mismatch.
common.activation: Candidate suggestions use the stated exact role/facet rule. Source-based taxonomy assessment is attributed judgment. Report unknown if source does not establish the relevant role/facet. Positive source selection is not itself a taxonomy fact. No satisfaction inferred.
common.allClauses: All listed clauses are required for the candidate instance. A subset is a partial mapping, not a fit for the full candidate. Record which clauses fail to express the local responsibility.
common.referenceMeaning: No domain-specific pack or new local clause may be introduced in this round. A missing parameter value alone may be evidence unknown; an essential parameter kind not in the schema is a semantic mismatch.
common.noEnforcement: These candidate documents do not add a mandatory requirement, CLI gate or executable oracle.

definitions.title: Validated input and explicit rejection
definitions.statement: At a declared input boundary, admissibility is decided before protected effects; rejected input produces the declared caller-visible outcome without effects outside the selected rejection policy.
definitions.applicability: A subject accepts external or less-trusted input and is responsible for an accept/reject decision before a protected operation. Mere transport, construction of input, or use after validation is not sufficient.

activation.roleEvidence: A source-assessed boundary facet requires an actual validation crossing, not simply a public function name.

parameters.subject: source address
parameters.admissibility: A finite set of literal values, field type/range/required-key constraints, or a versioned declarative schema/grammar reference. Not an arbitrary semantic predicate or executable validator reference.
parameters.rejection: one of: throw-error, return-tagged-error, report-and-skip-record, reject-entire-batch
parameters.errorObservation: existing exception/result/report address plus literal rejection tag or code

clauses.statement: Every input in the declared domain receives an admissible/rejected decision using the same declared admissibility constraints before its protected effects.
clauses.falsifier: An input violating a declared constraint reaches a protected effect, or an admissible input is rejected by an undeclared constraint.
clauses.recipe: Derive valid and invalid inputs from each declared constraint and observe both decision and protected-effect trace.

clauses.statement: Rejected input follows exactly the selected rejection outcome and effect policy; rejected records cannot produce accepted-record effects.
clauses.falsifier: A rejected record changes protected state, a rejected batch publishes partial state, or rejection is reported as success.
clauses.recipe: Inject a rejection at the beginning and after accepted records; compare visible outcome and protected state against the selected mode.

clauses.statement: Rejection carries the declared caller-visible error tag/code or report entry, and is distinguishable from a successful empty result.
clauses.falsifier: A rejected input is indistinguishable from accepted-empty output at the declared caller observation.
clauses.recipe: Compare accepted-empty and rejected-input observations without consulting internal logs.

limits: Not arbitrary semantic validation, authorization, security certification, or validation of an entire call graph.
No implicit compensation, distributed transaction, partial in-record mutation or fail-open policy is represented by these modes.

definitions.title: Repeatable observable results
definitions.statement: Equal declared effective inputs produce equal declared observable results, including failures, under a fixed declared equality relation.
definitions.applicability: The subject promises repeatability of computed/transformed/selected output given effective inputs. Mere existence of inputs and outputs does not establish that promise; inherently exploratory, random or timing-dependent behavior is not assumed deterministic.

activation.roleEvidence: Facet requires source evidence of repeatable processing, with ambient effects either absent or captured as explicit inputs.

parameters.subject: source address
parameters.effectiveInputs: nonempty list of argument, prior-state, configuration and environment snapshot addresses fixed before comparison
parameters.observations: nonempty list of externally relevant return/output/state-change trace addresses for this operation; may not exclude an observation merely because it varies
parameters.equality: one of: exact-bytes, structural-value, ordered-sequence, unordered-set, unordered-multiset
parameters.errors: existing error/result observation address, or literal no-error-result if the declared operation has no error channel

clauses.statement: Two executions with equal effective inputs yield equal observations under the frozen equality relation.
clauses.falsifier: Equal input snapshots yield unequal declared output or state-change observations.
clauses.recipe: Replay a captured input snapshot while varying irrelevant process state and scheduling; compare all declared observations under the selected equality.

clauses.statement: Every clock/randomness/configuration/prior-state dependency capable of changing those observations is absent or named in effectiveInputs before execution.
clauses.falsifier: Changing an undeclared ambient value changes output while every declared effective input stays equal.
clauses.recipe: Inspect dependency reads and perturb each ambient source independently; do not add a newly discovered dependency to this frozen instance.

clauses.statement: Success versus failure and the declared error value are repeatable for equal effective inputs; an unobserved failure cannot be discarded from the comparison.
clauses.falsifier: Repeated equal inputs alternate between success/failure or different observable errors.
clauses.recipe: Repeat both normal and failing cases, preserving every result rather than filtering unsuccessful runs.

limits: Does not establish purity, termination, numerical accuracy, performance, or independence from explicit inputs.
Approximate numeric equivalence, probabilistic reproducibility and custom semantic equivalence are outside this revision.

definitions.title: Accounted structural projection
definitions.statement: A transformation preserves declared identities and fields for its supported source population, with every exclusion or approximation explicit and without inventing source authority.
definitions.applicability: The subject transforms an existing representation into another whose declared identities/fields can be preserved through selection, field copying/renaming and reordering. It is not applicable merely because it returns a value. Semantic lowering requiring new computations may expose a scope mismatch for this revision.

activation.roleEvidence: Role requires an actual transformation of an established representation, not parsing external syntax or declaring types. The inherited role is broader than this candidate's bounded clause schema; do not narrow the activation rule after observing a case.

parameters.subject: source address
parameters.identityFields: nonempty list of source field paths with corresponding target field paths
parameters.fieldMappings: list of sourcePath/targetPath pairs, with operation one of copy or rename
parameters.selection: when declared-selection: finite enum membership or field-presence/range constraints only; otherwise none
parameters.sortFields: field paths and ascending/descending directions, or empty
parameters.approximation: none or literal field-precision truncation with explicit precision and visible disclosure address

clauses.statement: Each supported source identity appears exactly once in output; any excluded source identity is refused or explicitly accounted for under the selected omission mode.
clauses.falsifier: A supported identity disappears/duplicates, or an excluded identity silently vanishes.
clauses.recipe: Compare identity multisets over the complete source population, including supported, excluded and malformed records.

clauses.statement: Mapped fields preserve their values under copy/rename, declared ordering and the only explicitly selected precision truncation; no other computation supplies their meaning.
clauses.falsifier: A retained field changes beyond the named operation, or preservation requires an unmodeled semantic transformation.
clauses.recipe: Compare every named field using distinct adversarial values and ordering ties; enumerate every declared approximation.

clauses.statement: The output cannot invent source identities or promote absent/unknown source evidence into an affirmative authoritative value.
clauses.falsifier: Output contains a source-attributed identity or affirmative evidence value that no source item supports.
clauses.recipe: Project empty, missing-evidence and mixed-known/unknown sources and inspect output identity/evidence attribution.

limits: Not a general semantic-equivalence proof for compilers, optimizers, numerical models or arbitrary aggregation.
One-to-many/many-to-one transformations, computed identity synthesis and custom preservation predicates are outside this revision.
A failed broad lowerer-role activation must remain a failure rather than be hidden by redefining the role.

definitions.title: Explicit durable authority and recovery
definitions.statement: A named persistence operation distinguishes authoritative data from rebuildable derivatives, publishes complete durable units under a declared failure model, and recovers without silently substituting missing or damaged authority.
definitions.applicability: The subject owns durable read/write/recovery or cache persistence with an explicit authority distinction. Merely holding process memory, formatting data for another owner to store, or calling an opaque save API without owning the policy is insufficient.

activation.roleEvidence: Facet requires source evidence of durable storage responsibility. It does not itself imply transactions or an adopted crash-recovery promise.

parameters.subject: source address
parameters.authority: nonempty list of authoritative file/store/record addresses
parameters.derived: list of rebuildable cache/index addresses, possibly empty
parameters.operation: one of: replace-snapshot, append-record, read-recover, derived-cache-publication

clauses.statement: Authoritative state and derivatives are explicitly distinguishable; missing/damaged authority cannot be replaced by a cache or interpreted as empty success except the selected first-adoption condition.
clauses.falsifier: Loss of remembered authority yields an empty healthy result, or a cache silently becomes the authority.
clauses.recipe: Remove or damage each authority and derivative independently; compare failure/first-adoption/rebuild behavior.

clauses.statement: The declared publication unit is all-or-nothing under the selected failure model; success is observable only after a complete unit is durably published.
clauses.falsifier: An acknowledged unit is absent/partial after recovery, or readers observe a partially published unit.
clauses.recipe: Interrupt at publication boundaries or present torn records, then read using the normal recovery path; preserve acknowledgments as evidence.

clauses.statement: Recovery follows the selected damaged-authority and derivative policy, and never silently treats rejected authority as an empty valid history.
clauses.falsifier: Recovery drops damage without disclosure, accepts a partial committed unit, or rebuilds from data not designated authoritative.
clauses.recipe: Exercise clean, missing, damaged and interrupted states; identify the exact recovered unit and the visible degradation/error.

limits: No distributed consensus, replication convergence, backup retention, multi-object transaction or arbitrary compensation policy.
A persistence facet alone does not establish these stronger publication/recovery responsibilities; a mismatch must be recorded.
Source-only inspection may leave durability or recovery evidence unknown; this is not permission to call missing tests a pass.
